The former vice president pointed to the profits Trump and his family have made through cryptocurrency ventures as a troubling concern for Americans.

Trends Reporter, HuffPost

Former Vice President Mike Pence criticized President Donald Trump’s administration Sunday on NBC’s “Meet the Press,” saying an “air of corruption” contributed to the GOP’s sweeping losses in the midterm elections.

“I am convinced our voters didn’t turn left. I think they were turned off,” Pence said.

Pence argued that voters were concerned about reports involving administration officials and the staggering increase in Trump and his family’s collective wealth since the president returned to the White House for his second term in January 2025.

“I think the air of corruption, one story after another about Cabinet officials, family members of Cabinet officials ... and the president’s first family themselves have just been troubling to the American people. I mean, literally,” he shared.

Pence pointed to the profits Trump and his family have made through cryptocurrency ventures as a particularly big concern for Americans.

“The president was a successful businessman long before he came into office and no one begrudges him or the Trump family to continue to be in business — but a billion-dollar increase in your net worth through cryptocurrency is astounding to Americans,” he explained.

Pence added, “And the fact that a large portion of the source of that, before the inauguration, came from foreign interests in the Arab world.”

The former vice president did not declare that Trump, who has reportedly made nearly $3 billion while in office, has done anything illegal or unethical. Transparency advocates have raised concerns about the profits, considering a bulk of the money comes from foreign sources.

Pence then warned that it is crucial for the GOP to “return our party to the conservative principles that essentially were synonymous with the Republican Party for 50 years.”

“But also, I think returning our party to the high standards in public office will be just as important,” he continued.
